title: Immunization Schedule calculateur
formula: See full schedule at the CDC's website for[children](https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/hcp/imz-schedules/child-adolescent-age.html)and[adults](https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/hcp/imz-schedules/adult-age.html).

how_to_use.when: Use for pediatric and adult patients to determine if they may be eligible for vaccination.
how_to_use.pearls:
- This calculator is meant to provide a general schedule of vaccination doses. Clinical judgment and knowledge of past vaccinations should guide the decision to provide vaccinations to patients.
- Be aware of appropriate interval dosing and catch-up schedules. Giving a vaccine prior to the appropriate interval may invalidate it and require revaccination.
- Live vaccines are ***contraindicated*** in pregnancy. If you are evaluating a patient who could be pregnant, ensure pregnancy is ruled out prior to administering a live vaccine.

next_steps.advice:
- Make sure to discuss vaccination and immunization safety with the patient, and have a full understanding of the patient's history before administration.
- Determine pregnancy status if administering a live vaccine. Live vaccines are **contraindicated** in pregnancy.
- COVID-19 vaccination recommendations change frequently; consult the[CDC website](https://www.cdc.gov/covid/vaccines/stay-up-to-date.html)for the most up-to-date information.
- Pneumococcal vaccination is now recommended for adults ages 50 and older.
- There are many pneumococcal vaccine options including pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV15, PCV20, and PCV21) and pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23); follow[CDC guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/pneumococcal/hcp/vaccine-recommendations/index.html)to ensure your patient receives the most appropriate vaccination based on their medical history.
- Be aware of specific pneumococcal vaccination recommendations from the[CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/73/wr/pdfs/mm7336a3-H.pdf)for those patients who live in areas with high rates of serotype 4 invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD).
